correctness.rationale: Rudin–Shapiro recursion implies all coefficients ±1 and |P_r|∞<=sqrt(2*2^r), hence sum g_m converges uniformly with norm <=sqrt2/16 and f>0. Distinct clusters [10m,10m+1/8) and reflections yield locally finite spectral support; compact-support test functions see only finitely many blocks, so distributional Fourier equality holds without absolute global spectral summability. Each q-powered cluster has mass 2^{m²(1-q/2)-qm-5q}, diverging for every 0<q<2, while q=2 masses decay and q>2 are pointwise dominated. Fourier convention and translation-bounded balls accounted for.
